hints: Notice that a yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine is the classic iodoform test, so think about what functional group gives this result.
Recall that an alcohol is positive only if it contains the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, which can be oxidised to $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$.
Look carefully at each cyclic structure and spot which one has a $\text{CH}_3$ attached to the same carbon as the $\text{OH}$ bearing carbon outside the ring.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the test**

A yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2(\text{aq})$ is $\text{CHI}_3$, iodoform. This is a positive triiodomethane test.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{ or } \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- + \text{I}_2 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3(s, yellow) + \text{other products}$$

**Apply the rule to alcohols**

For an alcohol to be positive, it must be either ethanol or a secondary alcohol containing the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group. On warming it is first oxidised to a methyl ketone, which then forms iodoform.

**Inspect the four structures**

Options A, B and C have the $\text{OH}$ directly on the ring or as $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, so they do not contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$. Only one structure has a side chain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ attached to the cyclohexane ring, so that must be alcohol X.

options.A: This is a secondary cyclic alcohol with $\text{OH}$ on the ring. The carbon bearing $\text{OH}$ is attached to two ring carbons, not to a $\text{CH}_3$ group, so it cannot form $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ on oxidation and gives no iodoform.
options.B: This is a primary alcohol, $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$. Only ethanol among primary alcohols gives a positive test because only it can be oxidised to ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$. This larger $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ cannot form a methyl carbonyl group.
options.C: This is a tertiary alcohol with $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CH}_3$ on the same ring carbon. Tertiary alcohols resist oxidation under these conditions, so no methyl ketone can form and the test is negative.
options.D: This is 1-cyclohexylethan-1-ol, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. It clearly contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit. It is oxidised to the methyl ketone $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{COCH}_3$, which then gives the yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate.
